notes: Fill in any <placeholder> with a current PR before running, since PR state changes. Run each prompt with and without the skill, from a checkout of the PR's head commit. Compare the Reviewer Briefs against the expectations. Never let an eval run push, edit a PR description or post comments: use update_brief.py --dry-run.

evals.prompt: I'm about to mark PR 777 (the OpenTelemetry spans one) ready for review. Run the pre-PR review on it and give me the Reviewer Brief, but don't touch the PR.
evals.expected_output: A brief that a reviewer who never saw the review can act on.
expectations: "Start here" names one file or function from the diff and says why it matters.
No section lists bugs that were fixed during the review, finding counts, open questions or lens names outside the footer.
"Where it could fail" has at most three items, each with a file and line, or a clearly named behaviour, and a concrete way it could go wrong.
"Not verified" names live provider APIs or cluster mode.
"Beyond CI" contains only checks CI does not run, or is omitted.
The footer names the reviewed commit, the agent and model, and the lenses that ran.
The visible brief is under about 200 words.
Any question the review could not settle is put to the user before the brief is written, and none appears in the brief or elsewhere in the PR.

evals.prompt: Quick one: I fixed a typo in a docstring in redisvl/query/filter.py and a broken link in docs/user_guide/how_to_guides/observability.md. Do the pre-PR review thing and write the brief.
evals.expected_output: A very short brief that scales to the change.
expectations: The brief is under about 60 words.
Nothing is invented to fill "Where it could fail".
The review does not raise findings about code the change did not touch.

evals.prompt: Bugbot left comments on PR <number of an open PR with unresolved Bugbot threads>. Go through them using the repo's review process and tell me what you'd reply to each. Don't post anything.
evals.expected_output: Each open point verified against the code and given exactly one outcome.
expectations: The agent lists the open feedback with scripts/open_feedback.py or an equivalent that respects resolved and outdated threads.
Each point gets exactly one of: fixed in <sha>, already fixed, invalid with evidence, duplicate, needs a decision.
Points that are already resolved on the PR are not re-litigated.
Nothing is posted to the PR.

evals.prompt: Check out the first commit of PR 790 (handle uncompressed SVS-VAMANA indexes) and run the pre-PR review on it as if you were about to open the PR. Fix what you find locally and show me the brief. Don't push or touch the PR.
evals.expected_output: The review cuts the test matrix down to the cases that fail without the fix.
expectations: The agent runs the new tests against the merge base's library code, in a separate worktree, and reports which new tests pass there.
The cases that pass on the base are deleted or folded, leaving a small number of tests that each fail without the fix.
The challenger keeps the redundant-test findings instead of rejecting them as style.
"Beyond CI" states the result of the base run.
No test is kept that pins a compression mapping the change doesn't touch.

evals.prompt: Check out the first commit of PR 829 (OPENAI_API_KEY fallback when api_config has no api_key) and run the pre-PR review on it before I open the PR. Don't push or touch the PR.
evals.expected_output: The review finds the sibling constructors and the undeclared behaviour change.
expectations: The agent greps redisvl/ for the same credential-lookup expression and lists the other vectorizer and reranker constructors that have it.
Each sibling site is either fixed or put to the user as a scope question; none is silently left.
The review notes that an empty or None api_key in api_config now falls back to the environment where it used to raise, and asks for it in Release Notes and the docstring.
The review asks for a test of the default path, with no api_config at all.
Any question about widening the PR's scope is put to the user, not written into the brief.
